title: MORE Words and Phrases
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; illustrated number translations suggested separately

entries.example: How much are the trainers?
entries.description: You ask this when you want to know the price

entries.example: The price is six pounds ninety-nine.
entries.description: What you must pay for something in a shop

entries.example: I'd like these shoes here.
entries.description: I like this shoe and this one too. I'd like ___ shoes here.

entries.example: I'd like those trainers over there.
entries.description: Not these here, but ___ over there.
A shop assistant asks this when you want to buy more things
A shop assistant says this when you come into the shop

entries.example: How much is the computer game?
entries.description: You play this on a PC

entries.example: She can't hear you. She has headphones on.
entries.description: You put these on your ears to listen to music

entries.example: I put my key on a key ring.
entries.description: A small thing on your keys, often with a little toy on it

entries.example: Can I buy this magazine?
entries.description: A thin book with pictures that comes out every week or month

entries.example: Can I have a new mobile phone?
entries.description: You carry it in your pocket and call your friends with it

entries.example: I ride my scooter to school.
entries.description: It has two wheels and you push it with one foot

entries.example: The sweets are one ninety-nine.
entries.description: Chocolates and candy

entries.example: A tin of chicken soup, please.
entries.description: A metal container for soup or beans
You say this when someone wins a prize or has a birthday

entries.example: You know the rules.
entries.description: Something you must or must not do in a game or at school

entries.example: His customers like to come to the shop.
entries.description: A person who buys things in a shop

entries.example: Have you got everything?
entries.description: All the things

entries.example: The things in this shop are very expensive.
entries.description: The opposite of cheap

entries.example: Mr Anderson sits on his chair and falls asleep.
entries.description: To start sleeping
You say this when you leave

entries.example: I'd like 20 kilos of rice.
entries.description: A polite way to say 'I want ...'
You say this when something is not a surprise

entries.example: Suddenly, she hears the doorbell.
entries.description: Very quickly and when you don't expect it

entries.example: There's an old shop in the town.
entries.description: A place with houses and shops, smaller than a city

entries.example: The horse picks up the food and walks away.
entries.description: To leave on foot

entries.example: You can try them on in the changing room.
entries.description: A small place in a clothes shop where you try things on
You say this when someone thanks you or asks for help: It's OK!

entries.example: How much are those socks over there in the window?
entries.description: Not here, but in that place

entries.example: All my socks are in the drawer.
entries.description: A box in a desk or cupboard that you pull out
You say this when something is good now and not bad any more

entries.english: What can I do for you?
entries.german: Was kann ich für dich/Sie tun?
entries.description: A shop assistant asks this: How can I help?
You say this when something is dangerous
You say this when someone must wait a short time
The minutes in one hour
